title: Greek Salad
subtitle: Classic horiatiki with tomatoes, cucumber, feta and olives
excerpt: The real Greek salad has no lettuce. It is a coarse chop of ripe tomatoes, cucumber, pepper and red onion, dressed simply with olive oil and scattered with feta and black olives.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic Greek horiatiki (village salad) preparations.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The vegetables can be cut up to 1 hour ahead. Dress and add the feta only just before serving.

content.text: Horiatiki means village salad, and it is the salad Greeks actually eat. The vegetables are cut into large chunks rather than finely diced: this is not a tossed salad but a composed one, dressed at the table. Use the ripest tomatoes you can find; out-of-season supermarket tomatoes will produce a flat result. The black olives are traditionally kalamata, which you can find in most supermarket deli counters. They are not listed as an ingredient slug here as that slug is not confirmed, so simply scatter them over the salad to finish.

items.prepNote: halved lengthways and cut into thick half-moons
deseeded and cut into rings or strips
optional; many Greeks use only olive oil

content.text: Prepare the vegetables. Cut the tomatoes into rough chunks: quarters for small tomatoes, eighths for large ones. Halve the cucumber lengthways, then cut across into thick half-moons roughly 1.5 cm wide. Deseed and slice the green pepper. Slice the red onion as thinly as you can.

Arrange the salad. Spread the tomatoes, cucumber, green pepper and red onion across a wide serving plate or shallow bowl. Do not toss: the point is a composed salad where you see each element. Scatter a generous handful of black olives (kalamata, drained) over the top.
Add the feta. Place the feta in a single large piece on top of the salad, or crumble it over if you prefer. In Greece the block is traditional.

Dress and serve. Drizzle the olive oil generously over everything. Add the red wine vinegar if using. Scatter the dried oregano over the top. Season with a little black pepper; the feta and olives provide enough salt. Serve immediately with bread to mop the dressing.

items.symptom: Salad is watery and the dressing slides off
items.cause: The tomatoes and cucumber released too much liquid after cutting.
items.fix: Salt the tomatoes and cucumber lightly after cutting and rest in a colander for 15 minutes. Pat dry before assembling. This draws out excess moisture without softening the texture.

items.cause: Feta is brined and some brands are saltier than others.
items.fix: Rinse the feta block briefly under cold water and pat dry before placing on the salad. Use less feta and more olive oil to balance.

items.cause: Raw red onion can be very pungent, especially out of season.
items.fix: Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat dry. This removes most of the sharpness while keeping the colour and mild onion flavour.
